The city at night is a canvas of light, each skyscraper a brushstroke of vibrant fluorescence against the deep indigo of the twilight sky, painting an urban masterpiece that wakes up as the rest of the world sleeps.

To understand the primary material of a candle, one must look past the flame itself to the substance that feeds it. A candle is primarily composed of wax, which acts as the fuel source. This wax can be derived from various sources, including paraffin (a byproduct of petroleum), beeswax (produced by honeybees), soy wax (made from soybean oil), or tallow (rendered animal fat). The wax is typically molded around a wick, usually made of cotton or paper, which draws the liquid wax up through capillary action to be vaporized and burned, creating the light.
